title: Round robin with a time quantum

blocks.text: Round-robin scheduling is preemptive: every process gets the CPU in cyclic order for a fixed time slice called the quantum.

receipt.quote: Round-robin scheduling is preemptive: every process gets the CPU in cyclic order

blocks.text: If a process's remaining burst is longer than the quantum, it is preempted and placed at the tail of the ready queue; if its remaining burst is shorter than or equal to the quantum, it releases the CPU at the end of that burst without waiting out the rest of the quantum.

blocks.text: Think of RR as a queue of tickets: whoever waits gets served next, but everyone gets handed the ticket back after `quantum` units if they are not done. The quantum is the fairness dial — small quanta feel responsive but spend more time on context switches; large quanta drift toward FCFS.
P0 (AT 0, BT 5), P1 (AT 0, BT 3), P2 (AT 0, BT 4) with q = 2: the schedule runs P0[0–2], P1[2–4], P2[4–6], P0[6–8], P1[8–9], P2[9–11], P0[11–12], giving average waiting time **6.67**.

blocks.text: A classic exam trap: if the last burst is shorter than the quantum, the process does NOT wait out the full quantum — it finishes early and the scheduler switches immediately.
